page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor using the arm64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It also includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several core workloads. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1519.49 and a multi-core score of 12133.23. Memory bandwidth is measured at 472.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 101.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance is relatively weak in certain areas, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 5256.58. Cryptographic and compression tasks show lower relative performance, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1091.32 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.33 GB/sec.

The combination of 64.0 GB of RAM and 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes the r6gd.2xlarge appropriate for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch space, such as database operations and caching layers. This is supported by a Passmark database operations score of 5295.54 and a Redis SET performance of 9.53 million operations per second. The custom ARM-based Graviton architecture offers a cost-efficient alternative to x86-based memory-optimized instances, delivering balanced resource density for memory-bound applications, though it is less suited for compute-heavy tasks like large language model inference or intensive single-threaded processing.
